manager_rule: When kelvin_unrouted > 0 in round R's result AND the compiler's candidate pool — after applying all normal exclusions from Rules 37, 38, and 39 — consists EXCLUSIVELY of nets whose net_absorption_count >= 3 (i.e., every net remaining in the pool is a fast-track-exclusion candidate whose exclusion has been suppressed only by Rule 39's pool-empty safety gate), execute the safety-gate bypass protocol: (1) override the Rule 39 safety gate for this round and allow the compiler's output to be empty (zero compiler stubs produced); (2) deliver ONLY Rule 33's force-injected Kelvin stubs to FR for this round, bypassing the absorber, spur-trimmer, and orphan-removal stages for those stubs per Rule 34's mandatory_kelvin_bypass semantics; (3) do NOT increment net_absorption_count for any net that was suppressed by the safety gate this round — they were not targeted and the count should not advance; (4) log 'safety_gate_bypassed_all_pool_nets_above_fast_track_threshold' with fields: (a) round number R, (b) the list of nets suppressed by the safety gate and their net_absorption_count values, (c) kelvin_unrouted value from round R, (d) the Kelvin force-stubs injected via Rule 33, (e) confirmation that zero compiler stubs were produced. Rationale: the Rule 39 safety gate was designed to prevent a completely empty compiler round, but when every remaining pool net has net_absorption_count >= 3 and is being kept only by the safety gate, those nets produce stubs that are absorbed with probability approaching 1.0 every round — they consume all compiler slot capacity while delivering zero net routing guidance to FR. A Kelvin-force-injection-only round is strictly preferable: FR receives the same Kelvin force stubs it would have received under normal dual-path operation, with no slot competition from absorbed-bound stubs and no misleading topological signal from repeatedly-absorbed non-failing nets. This rule is additive to Rules 33, 34, 37, 38, 39, 40, 41, and 42; it shares net_absorption_count state without modifying it beyond clause (3); it fires before Rule 33 force-injection is appended for the current round; and it does not suppress any action those rules independently mandate for other cables or conditions in the same round.
